```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
penguins_clean <- na.omit(penguins)

```

## Overview & Motivation

Morphological features are key indicators of health and ecological adaptations in polar penguin populations.

* **Objective:** Provide an interactive tool estimating penguin body mass in grams ($g$).
* **Dataset:** Built on `palmerpenguins::penguins` curated by Dr. Kristen Gorman.
* **Predictors:**
* Species (`species`)
* Flipper Length (`flipper_length_mm`)
* Bill Length (`bill_length_mm`)



## Dataset Inspection

Data summary of clean observations across three species in the Palmer Archipelago:

```{r dataset_summary, echo = TRUE}
head(penguins_clean[, c("species", "flipper_length_mm", "bill_length_mm", "body_mass_g")], 4)

```

## Regression Model Evaluation

A multiple linear regression model is fitted dynamically on biological metrics:

```{r fit_model, echo = TRUE}
fit <- lm(body_mass_g ~ species + flipper_length_mm + bill_length_mm, 
          data = penguins_clean)
summary(fit)$coefficients

```

The model demonstrates strong predictive power, accounting for species baseline differences alongside body dimensions.

## Application Architecture

The Shiny application executes real-time calculations using a responsive UI:

1. **User Interface (`ui.R` / `app.R`):**
* Dropdown menu for selecting species (*Adelie*, *Chinstrap*, *Gentoo*).
* Sliders for flipper length and bill length inputs.
* Light blue thematic styling using custom CSS rules.


2. **Server Calculations (`server.R` / `app.R`):**
* Evaluates target weight against trained linear regression parameters.
* Plots prediction point dynamically using a single-row data frame to avoid mapping warnings.
